title: Small change - big consequence: The impact of C15-C16 double bond in a D‑ring of estrone on estrogen receptor activity.
authors: Vonka, Petr; Rarova, Lucie; Bazgier, Vaclav; Tichy, Vlastimil; Kolarova, Tamara; Holcakova, Jitka; Berka, Karel; Kvasnica, Miroslav; Oklestkova, Jana; Kudova, Eva; Strnad, Miroslav; Hrstka, Roman
journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接筛选雌激素受体配体并实验验证，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接，但对象为类固醇小分子与ER，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法创新，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: Estrogen receptor alpha (ER) is a key biomarker for breast cancer, and the presence or absence of ER in breast and other hormone-dependent cancers decides treatment regimens and patient prognosis. ER is activated after ligand binding - typically by steroid. 2682 steroid compounds were used in a molecular docking study to identify novel ligands for ER and to predict compounds that may show anticancer activity. The effect of the most promising compounds was determined by a novel luciferase reporter assay. Two compounds, 7 and 12, showing ER inhibitory activity comparable to clinical inhibitors such as tamoxifen or fulvestrant were selected. We propose that the inhibitory effect of compounds 7 and 12 on ER is related to the presence of a double bond in their D-ring, which may protect against ER activation by reducing the electron density of the keto group, or may undergo metabolism leading to an active compound. Western blotting revealed that compound 12 decreased the level of ER in the breast cancer cell line MCF7, which was associated with reduced expression of both isoforms of the progesterone receptor, a well-known downstream target of ER. However, compound 12 has a different mechanism of action from fulvestrant. Furthermore, we found that compound 12 interferes with mitochondrial functions, probably by disrupting the electron transport chain, leading to induction of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway even in ER-negative breast cancer cells. In conclusion, the combination of computational and experimental methods shown here represents a rapid approach to determine the activity of compounds towards ER. Our data will not only contribute to research focused on the regulation of ER activity but may also be useful for the further development of novel steroid receptor-targeted drugs applicable in clinical practice.
abstract_zh: 雌激素受体α（ER）是乳腺癌的关键生物标志物，其在乳腺及其他激素依赖性癌症中的存在与否决定了治疗方案和患者预后。ER在配体结合后被激活，通常由类固醇触发。本研究采用分子对接（molecular docking）方法，对2682种类固醇化合物进行了筛选，以识别ER的新型配体，并预测可能具有抗癌活性的化合物。通过一种新型荧光素酶报告基因实验，测定了最具潜力化合物的效应。筛选出两种化合物7和12，它们表现出与临床抑制剂如他莫昔芬或氟维司群相当的ER抑制活性。我们提出，化合物7和12对ER的抑制作用与其D环中的双键有关，该双键可能通过降低酮基的电子密度来防止ER激活，或可能经过代谢生成活性化合物。Western blotting结果显示，化合物12降低了乳腺癌细胞系MCF7中ER的水平，这与孕激素受体（ER已知的下游靶标）两种亚型表达减少相关。然而，化合物12的作用机制与氟维司群不同。此外，我们发现化合物12干扰线粒体功能，可能通过破坏电子传递链，即使在ER阴性乳腺癌细胞中也诱导内源性凋亡途径。总之，本文展示的计算与实验方法相结合，为快速测定化合物对ER的活性提供了一种途径。我们的数据不仅有助于聚焦于ER活性调控的研究，也可能对进一步开发适用于临床实践的新型类固醇受体靶向药物具有价值。
